title: Woodland Lakes & Winding Paths
lead: For those who want to step deep into the pine woods and forget about city life for a while. Slow travel through the Tuchola Forest — the largest pine forest complex in Poland.
body:
Why the Tuchola Forest, differently

The Tuchola Forest is the largest pine forest complex in Poland — over 3,000 km² of forests, lakes and peat bogs, stretching between the Vistula and Brda rivers, south of Tuchola. It is a land where the scent of resin and pine needles becomes the strongest stimulus, muffling the noise of everyday life. This is a place where nature has still preserved its original, raw form.

Slow travel through the Tuchola Forest is a journey through a forest that does not overwhelm but invites you to slowly discover. A walk among forest reserves is a lesson in mindfulness. When you walk on a soft, needle-covered carpet and the only sound is the tapping of a woodpecker and the whisper of treetops, you can feel body and mind entering a state of deep relaxation. This is a land that rewards those who slow down — the longer you are here, the more details you notice: animal tracks, hidden lakes, rare plants.

What to see

The Tuchola Forest splits into several parts: Tuchola Forest National Park (centre), Zabory Landscape Park (north), Wda Landscape Park (east) and Tuchola Landscape Park (south). Three to four days are best to visit.

Tuchola Forest National Park

  • Tuchola Forest National Park — established in 1996, covers a fragment of the Tuchola Forest with lobelia lakes. The park's symbol is the lobelia lakes — unique water bodies with very clean water, where rare plants grow, including the water lobelia.
  • Lake Charzykowskie — one of the largest lakes in the region, a paradise for sailors and kayakers. In summer, regattas are held here, and in winter — iceboat races on the ice.
  • Kulawa River Valley Reserve — a reserve protecting the Kulawa river valley, with peat bogs and rare plants. Entry only on marked trails.
  • Nature trail by Lake Charzykowskie — an educational trail, leading through various habitats. Good for families with children.

Lakes and rivers

  • Brda and Koronowski Reservoir — the Brda river and the artificial Koronowski reservoir, popular among kayakers and sailors. Worth floating down the Brda — the route leads through forests and lakes.
  • Lake Wdzydze — called the Kashubian Sea, a complex of lakes connected by the Wda river. Worth it for sailors and nature lovers.
  • Wda River — one of the most beautiful rivers in the region, with numerous meanders and wild banks. Worth a kayak trip.
  • Lake Świt — a small lobelia lake, one of the most valuable in the park. Entry only on marked trails.

Villages and culture

  • Wdzydze Kiszewskie — a village with the Kashubian Ethnographic Park, one of the oldest open-air museums in Poland. Worth visiting for understanding Kashubian culture.
  • Tuchola — a small town in the centre of the Tuchola Forest, with a market square and accommodation base. Worth a walk and shopping.
  • Chojnice — a town with historic walls and a basilica, in the west of the region. Worth a walk.
  • Świecie on the Vistula — a small town with the ruins of a Teutonic castle, in the east of the region.
  • Osiek on the Noteć — a village with a Gothic church and the atmosphere of an old settlement.

Lesser-known corners

  • Krzywe Koło Reserve in the Wda Loop — a reserve in the Wda valley, with river meanders and unique vegetation.
  • Zabory Landscape Park — a park in the north of the Tuchola Forest, with lakes and forests. Less known than the National Park but equally beautiful.
  • Village of Leśno — a small village with a wooden church and the atmosphere of an old settlement.
  • Wda kayak trail — a kayak trail on the Wda river, leading through lakes and forests. Worth it for those who want to escape crowds.
  • Village of Czarna Woda — a settlement on the edge of the Forest, with a former railway station and atmosphere.

When to go

  • May and June — the best time for slow travel. Forests bloom, fewer tourists, long days. Worth a walk and kayak trip.
  • July and August — peak season. Lakes full, but still fewer crowds than by the sea. Worth it for swimming and water sports.
  • September — second best. Warm days, fewer people, mushrooms in the forests. September is a good time for a walk.
  • October — end of the season. Forests are quiet, but rentals may be closed. Worth it for those who have their own equipment.
  • November–April — winter in the Tuchola Forest is quiet and harsh. Worth it for those who seek solitude.

Getting there

  • By car: ~1.5 hours from Gdańsk (A1 and DK22), ~1 hour from Bydgoszcz (DK25), ~2.5 hours from Poznań (S5 and DK25).
  • By train: stations in Tuchola, Chojnice and Świecie on the Vistula, with connections from Gdańsk, Bydgoszcz and Poznań.
  • By bus: PKS and private operators from Gdańsk, Bydgoszcz, Poznań.

Public transport in the region is sparse — a car or bike makes moving between lakes and villages much easier.

How much time you need

A weekend (2 days) is the minimum — one day for a walk in the forest, one for a kayak trip or a swim in a lake.

Three to four days is realistic for a first visit. Two days for a Wda or Brda kayak trip, one for the National Park, one for the open-air museum in Wdzydze Kiszewskie.

A week lets you explore the entire Tuchola Forest — all parks, lakes, kayak and cycling trails, villages and open-air museums.

What to eat and where to sleep

  • Lake fish — whitefish, bream, pike. Smoked or fried, available in local fish shops.
  • Kashubian cuisine — herring in oil, smoked eel, Kashubian broth. Worth trying in local inns.
  • Mushrooms — in season (August–October) local restaurants offer dishes with mushrooms collected in the forest.
  • Beer from local breweries — several craft breweries in the region.
  • Coffee and cake — Tuchola and Chojnice have several good cafés.
  • Kociewie and Kashubian cheeses — local cheeses, available in regional shops.

Accommodation: Tuchola (largest choice, region centre), Charzykowy (on Lake Charzykowskie), Wdzydze Kiszewskie (close to the open-air museum), Chojnice (town, more options), agritourism farms in villages (quiet, cheaper). Book ahead in summer season.

Practical tips

  • Bookings — book campsites by the lakes in advance in summer season.
  • Kayak — kayak rentals operate in Charzykowy, Tuchola and along the Brda and Wda rivers. Book a kayak in advance for longer trips.
  • Weather — weather in the region can be changeable. Even in July, bring a rain jacket.
  • Mosquitoes and ticks — forests and lakes are paradise for mosquitoes and ticks. Repellent and mosquito net — essential.
  • Drinking water — water from the lakes is not drinkable. Bring a supply of drinking water.
  • Signal — good in Tuchola and Chojnice, weak or absent deep in the forest. Have an offline map.
  • Car parks — paid car parks at lakes and trails. They fill quickly in season.
tip: Visit the Tuchola Forest on a weekday to avoid the crowds and feel true isolation from the outside world. It is the best way to achieve a complete mental reset.
